question.leadin: Answer the following about the Conway Cabal.
question.text: One member of the Conway Cabal, James Wilkinson, was later involved in the possibly-treasonous activities of this man, who narrowly lost to Jefferson in the 1800 presidential election and shot Alexander Hamilton in a duel.
question.clue: This man detailed his move to Texas in a compromising "Cipher letter" sent to the first Governor of the Louisiana Territory, James Wilkinson.

swap.leadin: This structure was initially derided as a "Folly" and a "Big Ditch," but it greatly reduced transport costs between the Atlantic Ocean and inland United States.
swap.text: Name this massive engineering project built between 1817 and 1825. It allowed ships to transport goods from the Hudson River directly to the Great Lakes.
swap.clue: The man who championed this structure was governor of New York when it was completed in 1825, and this structure was sometimes denigrated as "Clinton's Folly."

question.text: In the early 19th century, British ships impressed American sailors into service and British forces supported Native American raids on American settlers; in Congress, War Hawks agitated until James Madison asked for the declaration of this war.
question.clue: Robert Ross was able to capture one side's capital city after the Battle of Bladensburg during this conflict.

swap.text: After rallying from a victory at Lake Erie, American forces were able to kill this Shawnee leader at the Battle of the Thames, destroying his Native American Confederacy.
swap.clue: Richard Mentor Johnson may have killed this man at the Battle of the Thames after this man helped capture Fort Detroit.

question.leadin: This politician created the Bureau of Indian Affairs.
question.text: Name this Senator, who advocated the doctrine of nullification. With Daniel Webster and Henry Clay, he was part of the Senate's "Great Triumvirate."
question.clue: This man wrote that the "right of judging" is an "essential attribute of sovereignty" in a document that he authored anonymously in 1828.

swap.leadin: Vermont Congressman Matthew Lyon was convicted of violating one of these laws.
swap.text: Name this set of Federalist-backed laws that stifled criticism of the government and made it more difficult for new immigrants to gain citizenship. They were created in an attempt to silence the Democratic-Republicans.
swap.answerHtml: Alien and Sedition Acts [prompt on a partial answer]
swap.clue: These laws required a 14-year pre-residency requirement before immigrants could become citizens.

question.text: Paying for these policies required levying often-unpopular taxes, including one that sparked this namesake rebellion in the Pennsylvania backwoods that was put down by a federalized militia under "Lighthorse Harry" Lee.
question.clue: During this event, the Mingo Creek Association protested with liberty poles.

swap.leadin: Along with setting aside land for universities, Manasseh Cutler advocated for this law to ban slavery in its jurisdiction.
swap.text: Name this 1787 law that organized townships in areas it authorized to eventually become new states.
swap.answerHtml: Northwest Ordinance [or the Northwest Ordinance of 1787; accept the Ordinance of 1787 or An Ordinance for the Government of the Territory of the United States, North-West of the River Ohio]
swap.clue: This law, which led to the appointment of Arthur St. Clair as provisional governor, built off of an ordinance from three years prior that established the Public Land Survey System.

question.leadin: During these conflicts, the ship Intrepid exploded, killing all 13 sailors on board.
question.text: Name these conflicts between the U.S. and pirates on the North African coast.
question.clue: Another began with the capture of the Meshuda at the Battle of Cape Gata after a declaration of war by Umar ben Muhammed.

swap.leadin: One death that occurred on this vessel was perpetrated by Joseph Cinque [sin-kay], who led many captives onboard in an uprising that killed Ramon Ferrez.
swap.text: Name this ship that was the site of a revolt, and eventually landed on Long Island, where the passengers were taken back into captivity.
swap.clue: African-American slaves on this Spanish ship led a mutiny against its crew. After the slaves were tried for their crimes on this ship, they were sent back to their native countries.

question.leadin: One person with this last name was given command of the New York department of the Continental Army by George Washington.
question.text: Name this surname of the elder of the first two New York senators. A woman with this [emphasize] maiden name helped establish the Graham Windham orphanage following her husband's death by gunshot at Weehawken.
question.answerHtml: Schuyler [or Eliza (beth) Schuyler Hamilton or Philip John Schuyler; reject “Hamilton” alone] (The lead-in refers to Philip John Schuyler, Eliza Schuyler’s father.)

swap.leadin: Andrew Jackson issued this executive order in July 1836 requiring the purchase of public land to be done in only gold, silver, or scrip.
swap.text: Identify this attempt to try to slow down land speculation and the circulation of paper money.
swap.clue: Cries to "rescind" this order were common during the Panic of 1837.

question.text: John Slidell was one of two diplomats arrested during the Trent Affair. Earlier, this president had sent Slidell to Mexico in a mission designed to provoke the Mexican-American War.
question.clue: During his presidency, Abraham Lincoln demanded this President show the exact location where American blood had been spilled.

swap.text: The events of the Panic of 1907 included the collapse of New York's third-largest trust, which was named after this word. A satirical 1809 history popularized this term for New Yorkers who had Dutch ancestry.
swap.answerHtml: knickerbocker [accept Knickerbocker's History of New York; accept Dietrich Knickerbocker; accept Knickerbocker Trust Company]
swap.clue: A character of this surname was held to have gone missing before the publication of an 1809 "history" that popularized his baggy-kneed pants.

question.leadin: Susannah Carter's book about a frugal one of these people heavily inspired the first American cookbook, The American Cookery, by Amelia Simmons.
question.text: Give this type of person that titles a book often considered the first southern cookbook, published by a member of the Virginia-based Randolph family, Mary Randolph.
question.answerHtml: housewife [or housewives; or The Frugal Housewife or The Virginia Housewife]

swap.text: The rebellion started after shots were fired at this Pennsylvania tax collector while he was leading a US marshal through the area.

question.leadin: This man reportedly declared "the faster the Germans become Americans, the better it will be," sparking the legend that he stopped German from becoming an official language of the US.
question.text: Name this man who allegedly suggested the title "Mr. President" and was the first Speaker of the US House of Representatives.
question.clue: This man, who was stabbed by his own brother-in-law after casting the deciding vote on the ratification of Jay's Treaty, and lost to Thomas Mifflin in the 1793 governor's election in Pennsylvania.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the Constitutional Convention.
swap.text: Seconding Gerry's proposal was this man, a lawyer who later defended Samuel Chase during his impeachment trial and Aaron Burr during his treason trial, and also argued for the losing side in McCulloch v. Maryland.
swap.clue: This "drunken prophet" from Maryland walked out of the Convention along with fellow state delegate John Mercer, protesting the opposition to a bill of rights. He later embraced federalism and argued on behalf of the state in McCulloch v. Maryland.

question.text: Along with the Great Comet of 1811, this 1812 event centered on the Missouri bootheel that caused the Mississippi to flow backwards was a sign that led Tecumseh to give the call to arms that resulted in the Creek War.
question.answerHtml: the New Madrid earthquake [prompt on earthquake or equivalents]
question.clue: This natural event was widely believed to have been caused by the contemporaneous Great Comet.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about related to the military career of Nathaniel Lyon FTPE.
swap.text: Lyon's first major military experience may have been in the second of this series of conflicts fought in Florida between 1817 and 1858 against a certain group of Native Americans led by Osceola.
swap.clue: This series of conflicts fought with the namesake Indian tribe in Florida, of which the most famous is the second, when that tribe was led by Osceola.
